changes.reason: doctor: thermometer brings illness and doctors to mind; a thermometer does not measure a doctor. Same-topic fits; execution words all on the row.
piano: music topic from composer; a composer does not write a piano. Same-topic fits.
brush: art topic from gallery; a gallery does not hold brushes as its collection. Same-topic fits.
cloud: rain falls from a cloud, so it belongs with drought/rain and is not carried to famine. Example-anchor fits.
kitchen: a recipe is used in a kitchen; belongs with recipe/meal, not carried to blueprint. Example-anchor fits.
ticket: going-to-a-play topic; a scene is not part of a ticket. Same-topic fits.
kite: flies in a breeze; belongs with breeze/gale, not carried to shower. Example-anchor fits. (Row held for a separate reason.)

umbrella: rain topic from shower; not a heavier shower. The tag fits this value. But see the row-35 hold: drizzle, retagged reversed-relation as 47 outline was, would have kept the only distractor that tests direction.

look: glance (short) to look (plain) to stare (long) parallels whisper to talk to shout; right direction, stops at the middle step. A genuine wrong-degree, and look is not a second answer because whisper:shout is extreme to extreme.
loud: a shout is loud; belongs with whisper/shout, not carried to glance. Example-anchor fits. Note: loud is an adjective where stare/look are verbs, so a child can drop it on grammar alone.
angry: sits on the annoyed-furious scale, so it belongs with the first pair and is not carried to pleased. Example-anchor fits.
smile: happiness topic from pleased; not a stronger feeling. Same-topic fits this value. See the row-38 hold: happy (wrong-degree) was available for this seat.
bread: flour is made into bread; belongs with wheat/flour, not carried to grape. Example-anchor fits.
vase: a potter makes vases, pottery topic; marble is the material in the example, not the product. Same-topic fits; the execution says so correctly.
cow: one of the cattle; belongs with herd/cattle, not carried to flock. Example-anchor fits.
judge: runs a trial; belongs with witness/trial, not carried to referee. Example-anchor fits.
goal: football topic from referee/match; a referee does not take part in a goal. Same-topic fits.
outline retagged reversed-relation: sketch comes before painting (earlier to later); outline comes before draft, so naming it runs later to earlier. Matches my pass-1 judgement that it is a reversal.

warm:scorching is mild to extreme; damp:soaked is mild to extreme; wet parallels hot, not scorching, so it is now a true wrong-degree. sunny belongs with warm/scorching (anchor). The second-answer fault is fixed and the key is unique.

whisper:scream is quietest to loudest voice; whimper:wail is quietest to loudest crying. Cry is the middle step (wrong-degree) and tears are crying topic (same-topic). The sniffle and roar ambiguity is gone; key unique. Minor: whisper also opens row 36.

The note and movement fault is fixed and verse is correct, but the rebuild breaks the row another way. poet and author are both writers, so the two distractors are the same kind of word and the key is the only non-person. A child can pick the odd one out without using novel:chapter. Replace one writer, for example with rhyme (same-topic). Do not use line, which is also a section of a poem.
country (second answer) replaced by spelling: a dictionary is used to check spelling (anchor), not what an atlas is a book of. Geography unchanged. Fault fixed; map unique.
mercy (second answer) replaced by fear: a coward is full of fear (anchor); fear is not the opposite of cruelty. Violence unchanged. Fault fixed; kindness unique.
dune (second answer) replaced by wave: waves belong with the ocean (anchor); a grain is not part of a wave. Camel unchanged. Fault fixed; desert unique.

hesitate:act replaced by the clean opposites forget:remember; believe is the opposite of doubt. memory belongs with forget/remember (anchor); worry is uneasy-feeling topic, not an opposite. The loose-pair and accept faults are fixed; key unique.

rows.reason: temperature, doctor, hour: thermometer measures temperature; doctor and hour are not measured by it; key unique.
symphony, piano, note: composer writes a symphony; a piano is an instrument and a note is a part; key unique.
paintings, brush, frame: a gallery holds paintings; a brush is a tool and a frame a fitting; key unique.
food, crop, cloud: a famine is a lack of food; crop is a source of food and cloud belongs to rain; key unique.
building, brick, kitchen: a blueprint is the plan for a building; brick is a part and kitchen a room for recipes; key unique.
play, ticket, line: a scene is part of a play; ticket and line wrong; key unique.
soaked, wet, sunny: warm:scorching is mild to extreme, so damp:soaked; wet is only the middle step; key unique under every reading; all words known.

downpour, kite, umbrella: downpour is the only kind of rain among the options. A child can pick it without using breeze:gale, so the row no longer tests the stronger-version relation. Drizzle was the one distractor that tested direction. Keep drizzle, retagged reversed-relation (lighter, not heavier), in place of umbrella.

stare, look, loud: glance to stare is shortest to longest look, as whisper to shout is quietest to loudest; look is the middle step and loud belongs to shouting; key unique. Note: loud is an adjective and can be dropped on grammar alone.

wail, cry, tears: whisper:scream is quietest to loudest voice, whimper:wail quietest to loudest crying; cry is the middle step and tears is a topic word; whimper, wail and scream are known to 9-11s; key unique.

delighted, angry, smile: no option is on the pleased scale except the key. Angry is a negative feeling and smile is not a feeling word, so a child can pick the only strong happy word without judging strength, which is what the row tests. Replace smile with happy, a genuine wrong-degree (annoyed, angry, furious parallels pleased, happy, delighted).
juice, bread, vine: wheat is made into flour, grapes into juice; bread is flour product and vine the source; key unique.
clay, vase, statue: sculptor works in marble, potter in clay; vase and statue are products, not materials; key unique.
sheep, cow, wool: a herd is cattle, a flock is sheep; cow belongs to cattle and wool is a part; key unique.

verse, poet, author: verse is correct and unique, but both distractors are writers. A child can drop the two people together and pick the odd one out without applying novel:chapter. Replace one writer, for example with rhyme.
map, spelling, geography: a dictionary is a book of words, an atlas a book of maps; spelling and geography are not what an atlas is made of; second answer removed; key unique.
kindness, violence, fear: cowardice is the opposite of bravery, cruelty of kindness; violence is a near-synonym and fear belongs with cowardice; mercy removed; key unique.
match, judge, goal: a witness appears at a trial, a referee at a match; judge and goal are not events a referee attends; key unique (the pair stays loose, as noted in pass 1).
desert, camel, wave: a drop is a tiny part of the ocean, a grain of the desert; camel and wave are not wholes a grain belongs to; dune removed; key unique.
essay, outline, pen: a sketch comes before a painting, a draft before an essay; outline comes before the draft and pen is a tool; key unique.

believe, memory, worry: forget:remember are opposites and doubt:believe are opposites; memory is a noun belonging to the first pair and worry is not an opposite; key unique. Note: memory can be dropped on grammar alone.
